title: Projectivity of a fixed saturated logarithmic blowup tower
statement: Let $T$ be a finite saturated logarithmic blowup tower [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with quasi-compact initial scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $p_i:X_i\to X_0$ be log morphisms, with $p_0$ the log identity [def-per-log-morphism-identity] and $p_{i+1}=p_i\circ b_i$ as log morphisms [def-per-log-morphism-composition]. Let $A$ be any commutative ring. Suppose $X_0$ admits a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ for some finite $n$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the underlying terminal composite $p_N$ is H-projective: it factors as a closed immersion into finite projective space over $X_0$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. No log regularity, integralness, terminal freeness, excellence or Noetherianity of $A$ is assumed. Length zero is allowed.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, pp.107--108; Stacks constructions and morphisms Tags 01N2, 01Q2, 01PU, 0BCL, 0C4P, 087S. The chart/polarization argument is the original parent steps 1 and 3--6.

proof.text: The initial scheme is quasi-compact by hypothesis and locally Noetherian by the fs interface, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. It also admits an ample invertible module. Indeed [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension], with the polynomial graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$, identifies $\mathbf P^m_B$ with $\operatorname{Proj}A[T_0,\ldots,T_m]$: the graded scalar-extension isomorphism sends $a\otimes T^e$ to $aT^e$, with inverse on monomials. Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-shrink-to-closed-exists] to the given immersion of the quasi-compact $V$. It factors as a closed immersion into a quasi-compact open $W$ of this Proj. By [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample], $W$ has an ample invertible twist; its restriction to $V$ is ample by [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion]. These conclusions use exactly the stated finite-projective-space convention.

source.place: Tags 01T6, 01OY; 01N2 (affine Proj scalar extension); 01MW and 01Q2 (ample twists), 01PU (closed restriction).

proof.text: Consider one stage and a strict affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ on its target, with fs chart $P$ and center generated by finite nonempty $E\subset P$. By [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], the fine blowup has charts $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e])$, $Q_e=\langle P,h-e:h\in E\rangle$. To see its local properness, put $R=\mathbf Z[P]$ and $L=(z^e:e\in E)$. In $\mathbf Z[P^{\rm gp}]$, the monomials of the subalgebra $R[L/z^e]$ have precisely the exponents $Q_e$; their linear independence identifies this ring with $\mathbf Z[Q_e]$. The charts of [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] therefore identify the fine blowup with the scheme base change of $\operatorname{Bl}_L(\operatorname{Spec}R)$. The identifications agree on overlaps: both invert $z^{f-e}$ and send every monomial to itself. Use [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] for this identification. The toric ordinary blowup is proper by [lemma-nagata-global-blowup-proper-local], since $L$ is finitely generated. Its base change is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. No equality between the fine blowup and the ordinary blowup of $C$ is asserted or required.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, toric chart construction; ordinary blowup charts and scalar extension, Stacks Tags 01N2 and 02NS.

proof.text: The saturated blowup is finite over the fine blowup by [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction]. Its strict etale restriction is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-morphism-fpqc-descent] to descend properness to every arrow. Properness includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Starting with the quasi-compact initial level, quasi-compactness of a proper morphism over a quasi-compact scheme inductively makes every level quasi-compact. All levels are already locally Noetherian by the fs interface and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9 (finite saturation); proper base-change and descent, Stacks Tags 02L1 and 01T6.

proof.text: For one saturated stage, still over a strict affine chart with center $E$, the pulled-back log ideal is locally principal. By [lem-trf-log-ideal-chart-lifting-criterion], the locus where $e\in E$ generates it is exactly its affine saturated chart, and the overlaps invert $z^{f-e}$. Apply [lem-trf-principal-log-ideal-tautological-polarization] to this locally principal ideal. It supplies an invertible module with local frames $v_e$, transitions $v_f=\alpha(f-e)v_e$, and global sections whose nonvanishing loci are precisely these affine charts; it is relatively ample over the affine base chart. The construction is independent of generators and is canonical under ideal-preserving log isomorphisms and affine base change, by the same cited statement. Consequently on intersections of strict etale base charts the resulting line bundles have canonical identifications satisfying the cocycle condition: each identification is the identity on the intrinsic sheaf of generators of the pulled-back log ideal.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, polarized descent of the chart construction, with the generator torsor of the pulled-back ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polarized-fine-log-etale-descent] to the polarized local schemes of the preceding step. The log schemes already glue to our saturated blowup by the chart construction, and uniqueness identifies the descended scheme with that blowup; thus it carries the descended invertible module. Relative ampleness descends by [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent], applied to this scheme and its ordinary invertible module, along the fpqc cover of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Each stage is therefore proper with a relatively ample invertible module over a quasi-compact quasi-separated target. By [lem-sfb-proper-relative-ample-projective-bundle] it is projective in the bundle sense. Iterate [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition] over the finite tower, with base $V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The composite $b:Y\to V$ is bundle-projective (for length zero use $\mathbf P_V(\mathcal O_V)=V$). Finally [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective], using the ample module on $V$ from the first step, makes $b$ projective in the required finite-projective-space convention. The initial identity and recursive CompEq equations identify the supplied p with these composites, by induction on Fin (length+1).

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, polarized etale descent; Stacks Tags 0D3C, 0BCL, 0C4P and 087S.

lean.statement:
theorem saturatedLogTower_isHProjective
    (T : SaturatedLogBlowupTower.{u}) [CompactSpace (T.level 0).scheme]
    (p : ∀ i : Fin (T.length + 1), EtaleLogHom (T.level i) (T.level 0))
    (hp0 : p 0 = EtaleLogHom.id (T.level 0))
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin T.length, (T.arrow i).CompEq (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (hqp : ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : (T.level 0).scheme ⟶
      ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); Spec (.of A))), IsImmersion i) :
    IsHProjective (p (Fin.last T.length)).base
